content: The oral mucosa refers to the mucous membrane epithelium that lines the interior of the mouth. It is categorized into three distinct types based on structure and function: 1. Masticatory mucosa: This type consists of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium. It is primarily located on the dorsum of the tongue, the hard palate, and the attached gingiva. These areas are subject to significant mechanical stress, such as during chewing, and the keratinization provides added protection. 2. Lining mucosa: This type is composed of non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium. It is found in most other regions of the oral cavity, including the inner surfaces of the lips, cheeks, the floor of the mouth, the ventral surface of the tongue, and the soft palate. Its non-keratinized nature makes it more flexible and less resistant to mechanical stress compared to masticatory mucosa. 3. Specialized mucosa: This type is specifically associated with the regions of the taste buds, which are located on the dorsum of the tongue. It plays a critical role in the sensory function of taste.
